title: Taking counsel (ch. 3)
hookLine: the whole community is called, because God often reveals the better way to the youngest

cards: The grown-ups have been going around in circles all evening: which car to sell, how to fit the move around school, who takes the dog.
Then the youngest at the table, spooning up a bowl of cereal, says the obvious thing nobody had seen. The room goes quiet. Somebody laughs.
And it's right, and everyone at the table knows it. Saint Benedict built that moment into the life of a monastery, on purpose.

teach.b: Chapter three of the Rule is short. Whenever something important has to be decided, the abbot calls the whole community together and tells them what's at stake. Everyone, not just the senior monks.
He listens to their advice, thinks it over on his own, and does what he judges best.

teach.h: GOD SHOWS THE YOUNGER WHAT'S BETTER.
teach.b: And here's Benedict's reason for calling everyone: the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. The newest monk, the one with the least standing, may be the one who sees it.

He tells the monks how to speak up: humbly, without stubbornly defending their own view. And he tells the abbot he'll answer to God for what he decides, so he should decide fairly. The final call is still his.
This isn't a vote. It's something quieter: a leader who has to hear the whole room before he chooses. The Bible has a story that fits.

In the temple, God's voice comes in the night, not to the old priest Eli, but to the boy Samuel. Eli tells him how to answer, and the boy says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth."

teach.h: A WEEK ABOUT WHO GETS HEARD.
teach.b: Look back at this week: Thomas's straw and his last days at Fossanova, many schools beside him, then Benedict's first word, listen; a school for beginners; an abbot who fits himself to each person; and now an abbot who listens to the youngest.

teach.h: SPEAK, LORD, FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.
teach.b: A whole week about who gets heard.

how: In Benedictine monasteries the abbot or abbess consults the community in chapter before major decisions, as chapter 3 of the Rule describes, and then makes the decision.

o: a private talk between the abbot and the eldest monks
the abbot hearing the whole community before deciding
a vote where the monks' majority makes the choice

p: God often shows the younger what's better
speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth

s: in chapter 3, the monks vote and the majority wins
the abbot hears everyone, thinks it over, and decides. it isn't a vote.
Benedict says the Lord often shows what's better to the younger
that's his reason for calling the whole community.
only the senior monks are called for important matters
the Rule calls the whole community for important business.

games.q: you're the abbot, facing a big decision. who do you call to advise you?
o: only the oldest and wisest monks.
the whole community, down to the youngest.
no one: the abbot decides alone.
games.why: Benedict says call everyone, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. then the abbot decides.

practice: Bring to mind a decision you're carrying, big or small, and then someone younger or newer than you: a child, a niece, a new hire, a friend just starting out.

Put the question the way you'd put it to them, one plain sentence with no background, and notice what drops away when it has to be that simple. If you pray, ask God to speak to you through whoever you least expect.

wordCard.voice: Taking counsel. In Benedict's Rule, the abbot calls the whole community before an important decision, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the youngest may be right. Sometimes the clearest voice in the room is the newest one. That's the week.

sources.q: Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.
